issue_context.title: kubectl edit invalid content will remove command interpreter which begin with `#`
issue_context.body:
### What happened?

1. create configmap, like 

```
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: test
  namespace: default
apiVersion: v1
data:
  foo.sh: |
    #!/bin/sh
```

2. kube edit  configmap test, and make some error and write-save, will see below

```
# configmaps "test" was not valid:
# * <nil>: Invalid value: "The edited file failed validation": [yaml: line 5: could not find expected ':', invalid character 'a' looking for beginning of value]
#
apiVersion: v1
data:
  foo.sh: |
aaa
```


### What did you expect to happen?

when the content after edited is invalid, should not remove data , thus mean expect content below 

```
# configmaps "test" was not valid:
# * <nil>: Invalid value: "The edited file failed validation": [yaml: line 5: could not find expected ':', invalid character 'a' looking for beginning of value]
#
apiVersion: v1
data:
  foo.sh: |
    #!/bin/sh
aaa

```

### How can we reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)?

1. create configmap

```yaml
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  name: test
  namespace: default
apiVersion: v1
data:
  foo.sh: |
    #!/bin/sh
```

2 edit configmap make invalid
